name: Hierarchical Timeline
description: Resizable hierarchical timeline for profiling evidence. Owns expandable rows, a profiling window, horizontal zoom, event selection, and shared Swimlane Task Bar rendering while leaving domain hierarchy and event semantics to consumer data.

source.visualContract: Generalized from the hierarchy, zoom, window, and event-selection behaviors validated in pangu-moe-trainviz/microbatch-lifecycle-swimlane-mock.html; business-specific PP/MB/activation semantics are deliberately excluded.

useWhen: Events must be inspected across three or more expandable hierarchy levels.
A selected profiling window drives aggregation in another linked visualization.
Users need fit-to-window and deep horizontal zoom without losing row identity.
Timeline events must link to Inspector evidence through stable IDs.
doNotUseWhen: The surface contains only one compact, non-expandable row.
There is no meaningful time, step, duration, overlap, or event ordering.
A real-time packet animation is the product question; this pattern represents captured or derived profiling events.

dataContract.rows: [{ id, label, parentId?, depth?, events: [{ id, start, end, label, displayName?, color?, sourceEventIds?, transactionId?, objectRefs? }] }]

rules: Consumers define the hierarchy; the pattern must not hard-code microbatch, pipeline, communication, rank, engine, or operator levels.
Use stable event IDs and sourceEventIds to connect this timeline to graphs, Sankey ribbons, and Inspector evidence.
Render event bars through PtoSwimlaneTaskPattern.drawTaskBar; do not duplicate task-bar geometry or tooltip styling.
The profiling window represents an aggregate interval, not live packet motion.
Keep product-level tabs, diagnoses, filters, and actions outside the pattern.
agentReuseRule: Load swimlane-task/pattern.js before hierarchical-timeline/pattern.js, then provide rows and events through render(). Do not copy the hierarchy, zoom, window, task-bar, or tooltip implementation into a business page.
